meta.title: The Disturbing Secret Behind Your Favorite Artists' Paint #shorts
meta.description:
Have you ever wondered what artists in the 1800s were actually painting with? You might want to sit down for this one. For centuries, a highly popular pigment called "mummy brown" was used by famous painters all over Europe. But this wasn't just a spooky name. To make this rich, fleshy-toned paint, manufacturers literally bought ancient Egyptian mummies, ground them up into a fine powder, and mixed them with pitch and myrrh. Artists loved it for its rich texture and transparency. It was used in countless masterpiece paintings that still hang in museums today. The crazy part? It only stopped being produced in the 1960s, and not for ethical reasons—they literally just ran out of mummies to grind up. Check your walls, and follow for more mind-blowing history secrets.
